The PTE vs TOEFL decision should begin with one question: which test does your chosen course accept? Difficulty comes second.

PTE Academic often suits students who respond quickly on a computer, prefer integrated tasks and want fast results. TOEFL iBT may suit students who prefer separate skill sections, adaptive Reading and Listening, and short practical communication tasks.

Students sometimes compare the tests for days before checking their actual course page. That is backwards. Confirm the requirement, take an official mock for each test, then choose the format in which you perform better.

If you are still exploring international study options, keep the test decision tied to your course shortlist.

Quick answer: Choose PTE Academic if you prefer rapid, integrated computer tasks and need results quickly. Choose TOEFL iBT if you prefer distinct skill sections, adaptive Reading and Listening, and broad traditional recognition. Neither test is universally easier; course acceptance and mock-test performance should decide.

Pearson describes PTE Academic as a single two-hour computer-based test. The current TOEFL structure uses adaptive Reading and Listening alongside fixed Speaking and Writing sections.



TOEFL vs PTE: Which Is Easier?

Neither test is easier for everyone.

PTE may feel easier if you type quickly, speak comfortably into a microphone and recover well when tasks change at speed. It often combines skills: you may listen and speak, read and write, or reproduce spoken language after hearing it once.

TOEFL may feel easier if you prefer clearer boundaries. Its current tasks include completing words, reading everyday and academic texts, building sentences, writing an email, joining an academic discussion, repeating spoken language and responding in a simulated interview.

Here’s the thing: your strongest English skill does not always identify the easier test. Your test behaviour matters. A fluent speaker who freezes when a timer appears may struggle with PTE. A careful reader may find TOEFL’s adaptive sections demanding.

PTE is more likely to suit you if you:

  • respond quickly and accurately;
  • prefer recurring task patterns;
  • maintain clear pronunciation under pressure;
  • are comfortable with integrated questions; and
  • need the possibility of a very fast result.

TOEFL is more likely to suit you if you:

  • prefer one skill section at a time;
  • understand academic and everyday English;
  • adapt calmly when difficulty changes;
  • write concise emails and discussion responses; and
  • want a large established university network.

Take an official sample or scored mock for both. A timed attempt gives a better answer than another candidate’s opinion.

What Changed in the Current Test Formats?

Older comparison pages may now describe the wrong test.

PTE Academic updates

Pearson added Summarize Group Discussion and Respond to a Situation to tests taken after 7 August 2025. The first asks you to explain a discussion between three speakers. The second asks how you would respond to a realistic situation.

PTE remains primarily machine-scored, but “AI-scored” does not mean humans never check a response. Pearson’s scoring guidance says some complex responses receive human expert review before the automated score is finalised. The current Speaking and Writing section has nine question types and lasts about 76–84 minutes.

TOEFL iBT updates

ETS changed TOEFL iBT on 21 January 2026. Reading and Listening became adaptive. Speaking now uses Listen and Repeat and Take an Interview, while Writing includes Build a Sentence, Write an Email and Write for an Academic Discussion.

The new TOEFL scoring system uses a 1–6 scale in half-point steps. During the two-year transition after January 2026, reports also show a comparable 0–120 overall score.

PTE vs TOEFL Test Format

Skill

PTE Academic

TOEFL iBT

Practical difference

Complete the Words, Read in Daily Life and Read an Academic Passage

PTE rewards fast processing; TOEFL adjusts difficulty

Listening

Eight task types; recordings normally play once

Responses, conversations, announcements and academic talks

PTE places strong emphasis on accurate listening and reproduction

Speaking

Read Aloud, Repeat Sentence, Describe Image, Retell Lecture and situation tasks

PTE has more formats; TOEFL has fewer, direct formats

Writing

Sentence building, email writing and academic discussion

PTE leans towards summarising; TOEFL includes practical campus writing

PTE allocates about 76–84 minutes to Speaking and Writing, 22–30 minutes to Reading and 31–39 minutes to Listening. TOEFL lists base times of about 30 minutes for Reading, 29 for Listening, 23 for Writing and 8 for Speaking. ETS advises allowing approximately two hours because directions and adaptive variation affect the full sitting.

Task count alone does not decide difficulty. PTE asks you to learn more recurring formats; TOEFL requires steady performance as its adaptive sections develop.

PTE vs TOEFL Scores by CEFR Level

PTE Academic reports scores from 10 to 90. TOEFL reports section and overall scores from 1 to 6, with the overall score calculated from the average of the four sections.

These ranges share a CEFR reference; they are not an official direct conversion. Universities set their own overall and component minimums. A programme may accept PTE 59 overall yet require 59 in every skill.

Applicants to Britain should check the English conditions for their exact UK course, not rely on a general score table.

Is TOEFL More Widely Accepted Than PTE?

TOEFL has the larger published network. ETS reports acceptance by more than 13,000 institutions in over 160 countries. Pearson reports more than 4,000 universities and colleges accepting PTE Academic, with particularly broad coverage in Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the UK.

Those totals provide context. One clear statement on your course page matters more than thousands of acceptances elsewhere.

United States

TOEFL remains familiar to American admission teams, although many institutions accept PTE. When creating an American university shortlist, check the programme page rather than the homepage alone. You can first identify US institutions that list PTE, then verify the course.

United Kingdom

Many British universities accept both tests, but requirements may vary depending on the institution and course. Applicants should check the specific English language requirements mentioned in their university offer conditions.

Anyone planning a UK study route should review the university’s entry requirements and confirm which English language test is accepted for their chosen course.

Canada

Australia and New Zealand

PTE has strong recognition in both destinations, while many universities also accept TOEFL. During an Australian course search, verify the university score first and the government requirement second.

How to Check Whether a University Accepts PTE or TOEFL

Before paying:

  1. Open the requirements for the exact course and intake.
  2. Record the overall score and every component minimum.
  3. Confirm the accepted test version and delivery method, including TOEFL Home Edition or PTE Academic UKVI where relevant.
  4. Check any separate requirements related to scholarships, academic eligibility, or professional registration.

Do not rely on a general university page when the department publishes its own criteria. Save a dated copy of the requirement, as course pages and entry criteria can change.

Results, Fees, Validity and Retakes

Fee information checked: 2 August 2026.

PTE results typically arrive within 48 hours. TOEFL scores appear in the ETS account three days after the test. Both are normally valid for two years.

Base fees vary by country, currency, tax and centre. Check Pearson’s local price finder and ETS’s location-based fee page when you book.

ETS currently lists US$49 for express registration, US$69 for rescheduling and US$29 for each additional score report. TOEFL includes reports to four institutions. Pearson lets candidates share a valid PTE score with as many institutions as required without an additional reporting fee.

TOEFL reports also include MyBest scores, combining the highest valid section scores from different test dates. Each institution decides whether to accept them. PTE reports each sitting separately.

A faster result does not always create a faster application. A university may need additional time to receive or verify a score, so leave a buffer.

PTE vs TOEFL for a 2027 University Intake

Work backwards from the earliest course or scholarship deadline.

List every accepted test, overall score, component minimum and final evidence date. Compare official mocks, then book your first real attempt about 8–12 weeks before the earliest deadline where possible.

For example, a student has six weeks before an Australian master’s deadline. The course accepts both tests, the student already exceeds the PTE requirement in mocks, and a nearby date is available next week. PTE is practical.

Add a US programme that explicitly lists TOEFL but not PTE, and the safer choice changes. The best test is the one that keeps the greatest number of suitable applications open.

PTE or TOEFL: Which Should You Choose?

Choose PTE Academic when every target programme accepts it, and you perform better in rapid, integrated computer tasks. It is particularly useful when quick results and free score sharing matter.

Choose TOEFL iBT when it covers more of your shortlist and the adaptive, section-based format suits your skills. It may be the safer traditional option for a broad US-focused application.

Use this order:

  1. course acceptance;
  2. university or programme requirements;
  3. overall and component scores;
  4. official mock performance;
  5. deadline and local availability; and
  6. total cost, including a possible retake.

When a course page looks outdated or the rules conflict, check the requirement with an adviser before booking.

Common Mistakes

Do not book a test before checking the requirements of your chosen university or institution. Avoid comparing PTE Academic with PTE Core, relying on outdated TOEFL 0–120-only guidance, overlooking component minimums, or assuming that meeting one requirement automatically satisfies all academic criteria.

Do not choose a test based only on the lower-looking number. PTE 59 is not easier than TOEFL 4 simply because 4 appears smaller. They use different scoring systems and should be evaluated based on the relevant requirements.

Finally, do not choose TOEFL Home Edition only for convenience without confirming whether your selected university or institution accepts that test format. TOEFL offers both test-centre and Home Edition options, but acceptance policies may vary between organisations.

Final Verdict

The PTE vs TOEFL decision comes down to acceptance, format and timing.

PTE Academic often fits fast, computer-confident candidates who prefer integrated tasks and quick results. TOEFL iBT often fits students who prefer separate sections, adaptive Reading and Listening, and broad traditional recognition.

Do not choose the test that strangers call easier. Choose the one accepted across your serious applications, confirm every component score and let your official mock results break the tie.



Frequently Asked Questions

Is PTE easier than TOEFL?

PTE may feel easier if you type quickly, respond well under strict timing and like recurring task patterns. TOEFL may feel easier if you prefer separate sections, adaptive Reading and Listening, and direct communication tasks.

Is TOEFL easier than PTE for speaking?

TOEFL uses Listen and Repeat and Take an Interview. PTE uses more speaking formats, including Read Aloud, Repeat Sentence, Describe Image, Retell Lecture, Summarize Group Discussion and Respond to a Situation. TOEFL may feel simpler if you prefer fewer formats.

Which is better for the USA, PTE or TOEFL?

TOEFL remains a traditional choice with broad US recognition. PTE Academic is also accepted by many American institutions. Choose the test listed by every serious programme on your shortlist.

Which test gives results faster?

PTE results typically arrive within 48 hours. TOEFL results normally appear three days after the test. PTE has a small typical speed advantage.

Can I use PTE instead of TOEFL?

Yes, when the university and programme accept PTE Academic and you meet the required overall and component scores. Acceptance criteria can vary by university, department, and programme requirements.

Can I take PTE or TOEFL from home?

TOEFL iBT Home Edition is available, but each institution or authority decides whether to accept it. PTE Academic is normally taken at an authorised test centre.

Does TOEFL MyBest help after multiple attempts?

It can. MyBest combines the highest valid TOEFL section scores from different test dates, but each institution decides whether to accept it. PTE has no equivalent superscore.

How long are PTE and TOEFL scores valid?

What TOEFL score appears in 2026 and 2027?

For tests taken from 21 January 2026, reports show scores on the 1–6 scale and, during the transition, a comparable 0–120 overall score.

Should I take PTE or TOEFL for a 2027 intake?

Check every course’s accepted tests and scores, compare official mocks and aim to take the first exam 8–12 weeks before the earliest deadline.
